summaryShort: This person may push you toward more than you feel ready for. One of you may want to move quickly, take the risk, and trust the outcome. The other may need more time, more information, or a clearer plan.
summaryDeep:
This person may push you toward more than you feel ready for.

One of you may want to move quickly, take the risk, and trust the outcome. The other may need more time, more information, or a clearer plan. The difference can be frustrating, but it can also be useful.

Together, you can balance each other out. One person is ready to jump. The other sees what could go wrong. When you listen to both instincts, you take better risks and make fewer avoidable mistakes.

The challenge is that you can start fighting each other instead of solving the problem. They think you are dragging your feet. You think they are making bad decisions. They push. You resist. Before long, you are arguing about who is right instead of figuring out what actually makes sense.

This connection works best when both people respect what the other is protecting. One of you is trying to make sure the opportunity does not pass. The other is trying to make sure you do not create a bigger problem chasing it. Stop arguing about speed and get clear on the goal. Once you know what you are actually trying to achieve, it becomes much easier to decide how fast to move.
